translations.text: In the beginning God made heaven and earth.
And the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the depths, and the Spirit of God moved over the waters.
And God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light.
And God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening and there was morning: one day.
And God said, “Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let there be a division between water and water.” And it was so.
And God made the firmament, and God separated the water below the firmament from the water above the firmament.
And God called the firmament Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning: the second day.

And God said, “Let the waters below heaven be gathered into one gathering, and let the dry land appear.” And it was so. And the waters below heaven were gathered into their gatherings, and the dry land appeared.
And God called the dry land Earth, and the gatherings of water he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.

And God said, “Let the earth bring forth grassy vegetation bearing seed according to its kind and likeness, and fruit-bearing trees producing fruit according to their kind, with their seed in them, according to their kind and likeness, upon the earth.” And it was so.

And the earth brought forth grassy vegetation bearing seed, which is over all the earth, and fruit-bearing trees producing fruit with their seed in them, according to their kind, upon the earth. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening and there was morning: the third day.
And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of heaven to give light upon the earth and to divide the day from the night, and let them serve as signs and for seasons, days, and years.”
And let them serve as lights in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth. And it was so.
And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars.
And God placed them in the expanse of heaven to give light upon the earth.
And to rule over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening and there was morning: the fourth day.
And God said, “Let the waters bring forth swarms of living creatures and winged birds above the earth along the expanse of heaven.” And it was so.
And God made huge whales and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that they were good.
And God blessed them and said, “Increase and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply upon the earth.”
And there was evening and there was morning: the fifth day.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: four-footed animals, creeping creatures, and wild animals of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.

And God made the wild animals of the earth according to their kinds, and the livestock according to their kinds, and all the creeping creatures of the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that they were good.

And God said, “Let us make humankind according to our image and likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of heaven and the livestock and all the earth and all the creeping creatures that creep upon the earth.”
And God made humankind in his image; according to the image of God he made him; male and female he made them.

And God blessed them and said, “Increase and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of heaven and all the livestock and all the earth and all the creeping creatures that creep upon the earth.”
And God said, “Look, I have given you every seed-bearing plant that produces seed upon all the earth, and every tree that has within it fruit containing seed for sowing; these shall be food for you.”
And for all the wild animals of the earth and all the birds of heaven and all the creeping creatures that creep upon the earth, which have living breath, every green plant for food. And it was so.
And God saw everything he had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.
And the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their adornment.
And on the sixth day God completed his work which he had done, and on the seventh day he rested from all his work which he had done.
And God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all his work which God had begun to do.
This is the record of the creation of heaven and earth on the day when God made the heavens and the earth.

And every plant of the field, before it existed upon the earth, and every grass of the field, before it had sprouted, for the Lord God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no human being to cultivate the earth.
But a spring rose from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
And the Lord God formed the man from dust of the earth and breathed into his face the breath of life, and the man became a living being.
And God planted the garden in Eden, toward the east, and placed there the man whom he had formed.
And the Lord God also caused to grow from the earth every tree beautiful to look at and sweet for food, and the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree for knowing good and evil.
And a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided into four branches.
The name of the first is Pishon. It is the one that flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
And the gold of that land is fine, and there are ruby and malachite stones there.
And the name of the second river is Gihon. It flows around the whole land of the Ethiopians.
And the third river is the Tigris. It is the one that flows opposite Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
And the Lord God took the man whom he had made and placed him in the garden of delight to cultivate it and care for it.
And the Lord God commanded Adam, saying, “You may freely eat from every tree in this garden.
But do not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for on the day you eat from it, you will surely die.”
And the Lord God said, “It is not good for this man to be alone. Let us make him a helper suited to him.”

And the Lord God also formed all the wild animals and all the birds of the heavens, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam named each living being, that was its name.
And Adam gave names to all the livestock and all the birds of the heavens and all the wild animals, but for Adam no helper like him was found.
And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept. And he took one of his ribs and filled its place with flesh.
And the Lord God made the rib which he had taken from Adam into a woman, and brought her to Adam.
And Adam said, “This now is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, because she was taken from her own man.”
For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and follow his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.
And both were naked, Adam and his wife, and they were not ashamed.

And the serpent was more cunning than all the wild animals on the earth which the Lord God had made. And the serpent said to the woman, “Why did God say, ‘Do not eat from any of the trees that are in this garden’?”
And the woman said to the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of this garden.
But about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, ‘Do not eat from it, and do not go near it, lest you die.’”
And the serpent said to the woman, “You will certainly not die.
For God knew that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil.”
And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, pleasing to the eyes, and beautiful to look at. She took some of its fruit and ate it, and gave some to her husband, who was with her, and they ate.
And the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
And they heard the sound of the Lord God walking there in the garden toward evening. Adam and his wife hid from the presence of the Lord God among the trees of the garden.
And the Lord God called Adam and said to him, “Where are you?”
And he said, “I heard your sound here in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid.”
And he said to him, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree—the only one from which I commanded you not to eat?”
And Adam said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me—she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.”
And the Lord God said to the woman, “What have you done?” And the woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

And the Lord God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you shall be cursed above all livestock and all the wild animals of the earth. You shall go on your chest and belly, and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.
And I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will watch for your head, and you will watch for his heel.”
And he said to the woman, “I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your groaning. In sorrow you shall bear children. Your turning shall be toward your husband, and he shall rule over you.”

And he said to Adam, “Because you listened to your wife’s voice and ate from the tree—the only one from which I commanded you not to eat—and you ate from it, the ground shall be cursed in your work. In sorrow you shall eat from it all the days of your life.
It shall grow thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread until you return to the earth from which you were taken, for you were dust, and to dust you shall return.”
And Adam named his wife Eve, because she is the mother of all the living.
And the Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.
And the Lord God said, “Look, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take from the tree of life, eat, and live forever—”
And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of delight to cultivate the earth from which he had been taken.
And he drove Adam out and settled him opposite the garden of delight. He commanded the cherubim and the flaming sword to guard the paths to the tree of life on all sides.
Adam lay with Eve his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. She said, “I have acquired a man through God.”
And she also gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of flocks, and Cain worked the ground.
And after some days, Cain brought an offering to God from the fruit of the ground.
Abel also brought an offering from the firstborn of his flocks and from their fat. And God looked with favor on Abel and his offerings.
But he did not look with favor upon Cain and his offerings, and Cain was deeply grieved, and his face fell downward.
And the Lord God said to Cain, “Why have you become sad, and why has your face fallen?”
“If you offer correctly but do not divide correctly, have you not sinned? Be quiet. He will turn to you, and you will rule over him.”
And Cain said to his brother Abel, “Come, let us go into the field.” And when they went into the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
And the Lord God said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” And he said, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
And God said, “What have you done? The cry of your brother’s blood calls out to me from the earth.”
“And now you shall be cursed upon the earth, which opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hands.”
“When you work the earth, it will no longer give you its strength. You shall be shaking and trembling upon the earth.”
And Cain said to the Lord God, “My punishment is too great for you to forgive me.”
“If you drive me today from the face of the earth, I shall be hidden from your face, and I shall be shaking and trembling upon the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
And the Lord God said to him, “Not so. Whoever kills Cain will incur sevenfold vengeance.” And the Lord God put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.
And Cain went out from the presence of God and settled in the land of Nod, opposite Eden.
Cain went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. He was building a city, and he named the city after his son Enoch.
And Irad was born to Enoch, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
And Lamech took two wives for himself. The name of one was Adah, and the name of the second was Zillah.
And Adah bore Jabal. He was the father of those who live in shepherds’ tents.
And his brother’s name was Jubal. He was the father who introduced songs and lyres.
And Zillah bore Tubal. He was a master craftsman, a smith in copper and iron, and Tubal’s sister was Naamah.
And Lamech said to his wives, Adah and Zillah, “Hear my voice, wives of Lamech, and listen to my words, for I killed a man for wounding me, and a young man for striking me.”
“For if vengeance for Cain is sought sevenfold, then for Lamech it is seventy-sevenfold.”
Adam went in to his wife Eve, and she conceived and bore a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has raised up another offspring for me in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.”
And Seth had a son, and he named him Enosh. He hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God.
This is the record of the creation of humankind. On the day when God made Adam, he created him in the image of God.
He made them male and female, and blessed them, and named them Adam on the day when he made them.
Adam lived two hundred and thirty years and fathered a son in his own likeness and according to his own image, and he named him Seth.
And Adam’s days after he fathered Seth were seven hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
And Seth lived two hundred and five years and fathered Enosh.
And Seth lived 707 years after he fathered Enosh, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
And Enosh lived 190 years and fathered Cainan.
And Enosh lived 715 years after he fathered Cainan, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enosh were 905 years, and he died.
And Cainan lived 170 years and fathered Mahalalel.
And Cainan lived 740 years after he fathered Mahalalel, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Cainan were 910 years, and he died.
And Mahalalel lived 165 years and fathered Jared.
And Mahalalel lived 730 years after he fathered Jared, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mahalalel were 895 years, and he died.
And Jared lived 162 years and fathered Enoch.
And Jared lived 800 years after he fathered Enoch, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.
And Enoch lived 165 years and fathered Methuselah.
And Enoch was pleasing to God for two hundred years after he fathered Methuselah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch were 365 years.
And Enoch pleased God, and he was nowhere to be found, because God had taken him away.
And Methuselah lived 187 years and fathered Lamech.
And Methuselah lived 782 years after he fathered Lamech, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days that Methuselah lived were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.
And Lamech lived 188 years and fathered a son.
And he named him Noah, saying, “He will give us rest from our work, from the toil of our hands, and from the ground that the Lord God cursed.”
And Lamech lived 565 years after he fathered Noah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Lamech were 753 years, and he died.
And Noah was 500 years old, and Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And it happened, when people began to multiply on the earth and daughters were born to them,
that the sons of God saw that the daughters of humans were beautiful, and they took wives for themselves from all those whom they chose.
And the Lord God said, “My spirit shall not remain in these humans forever, because they are flesh, and their days shall be 120 years.”
There were giants on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men and they bore them sons. These were the giants of old, men of renown.
And the Lord God saw that human wickedness had increased on the earth, and that everyone deliberately planned evil in his heart every day.
And God regretted that he had made mankind on the earth, and he was troubled in his heart.

And the Lord God said, “I will wipe away all flesh that I have made from the face of the earth, from humans to livestock, and from creeping creatures to the birds of heaven, for I am angry that I made them.”
But Noah found favor before the Lord God.
These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation, and Noah was pleasing to God.
And Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And the earth became corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with injustice.
And the Lord God saw the earth, and it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
And the Lord God said to Noah, “The time of all mankind has come before me, for the earth is filled with injustice because of them. And behold, I will destroy them and the earth.
Now make yourself an ark from squared timbers. Make compartments in the ark, and coat it inside and outside with pitch.
Make the ark in this way: the length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
Make the ark taper, and finish it to a cubit at the top. Put the door of the ark in its side, and make lower, middle, and upper stories in it.
And behold, I will bring a flood of water upon the earth to destroy all flesh under heaven in which there is the breath of life. Everything on the earth shall perish.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall enter the ark—you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
And from all livestock, all wild animals, and all flesh, bring two of each into the ark to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.

Of all winged birds according to their kinds, all livestock according to their kinds, and all creeping creatures of the earth according to their kinds, two of each shall come to you to be fed with you, male and female.
And take for yourself some of every kind of food that you eat, and gather it to yourself. It shall be food for you and for them.”
And Noah did everything that the Lord God commanded him; so he did.
And the Lord God said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen that you are righteous before me in this generation.
Of all clean livestock, bring seven of each with you, male and female; and of all livestock that are not clean, two of each, male and female.
Also, of the clean birds of heaven, seven of each, male and female; and of the birds that are not clean, two of each, male and female, to preserve offspring over the whole earth.
For in seven more days I will bring rain upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe away every living thing that I have made from the face of the earth.”
And Noah did everything that the Lord God commanded him.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came upon the earth.
And Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives went with him into the ark because of the floodwaters.
And from the clean birds and from the birds that were not clean, and from the clean animals and from the animals that were not clean, and from all the creeping creatures that creep upon the earth.
They went to Noah into the ark two by two, male and female, as the Lord God had commanded him.
And after seven days, the floodwaters came upon the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, all the springs of the vast depths burst open, and the floodgates of heaven opened.
And rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that day Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah’s sons, and Noah’s wife and his sons’ three wives went with him into the ark.

They and every wild animal according to its kind, and all livestock according to their kinds, and every creeping creature that moves upon the earth according to their kinds, and every flying bird according to its kind.
They went to Noah into the ark two by two, from all flesh in which there was the breath of life.
Those that entered went in male and female, from all flesh, as God had commanded Noah. And the Lord God shut the ark from the outside.
And the flood was upon the earth for forty days and forty nights. The water increased and lifted the ark, and it rose above the earth.
And the water rose and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark moved upon the waters.
And the water grew very, very strong upon the earth and covered all the high mountains beneath heaven.
The water rose fifteen cubits higher and covered all the mountains.
And all flesh that moved upon the earth died: birds, livestock, wild animals, every creeping creature that swarmed upon the earth, and every human being.
Everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils, and everything that was on dry land, died.

And he wiped out every living thing that was upon the face of the earth, from humans to livestock, and from creeping creatures to the birds of heaven. They were wiped out from the earth. Only Noah remained, and those who were with him in the ark.
And the water rose upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Noah and all the wild animals, all the livestock, and all the birds that were with him in the ark. God brought a wind over the earth, and the water subsided.
And the springs of the depths and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the rain from heaven was stopped.
And the water gradually receded and withdrew from the earth, and the water diminished after one hundred and fifty days.
And the ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat.
And the water continued to diminish until the tenth month. In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
And after forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.
And he released the raven. It went out and did not return until the water had dried up from the earth.
And he released the dove after it to see whether the water had gone down from the face of the earth.

And the dove, finding no resting place for its feet, returned to him in the ark, because water still covered the whole surface of the earth. And he stretched out his hand and received it and brought it back to himself in the ark.
And he waited another seven days and again released the dove from the ark.
And the dove returned to him toward evening, carrying an olive sprig with a leaf in its mouth. And Noah knew that the waters had gone down from the earth.
And he waited seven more days and again released the dove, and it no longer returned to him.

In the six hundred and first year of Noah’s life, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the water receded from the face of the earth. Noah opened the roof of the ark he had made and saw that the water had receded from the face of the earth.
In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth dried out.
The Lord God spoke to Noah and said:
“Come out of the ark, you and your wife, your sons and your sons’ wives with you.

Bring out with you every wild animal that is with you, every living creature, from birds to livestock, and every crawling creature that moves on the earth. Let them teem on the earth, and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.”
Noah came out, with his wife, his sons, and his sons’ wives.
Every wild animal, every crawling creature that moves, and every bird on the earth came out of the ark according to their kinds.
Noah built an altar to God. He took some of every kind of clean animal and every kind of clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

The Lord God smelled the pleasing aroma, and the Lord God said within himself, “I will never again curse the earth because of human deeds, for the human mind is set on evil concerns from youth. Nor will I ever again strike down every living creature as I have done.
From now on, for all the days of the earth, sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and spring, day and night shall not cease.”
God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and rule over it.
Fear and dread of you shall be upon every wild animal of the earth, every bird of the sky, every creature that moves on the earth, and every fish of the sea. I have put them into your hands.
Every moving creature that is alive shall be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I have given you everything.
But you shall not eat flesh with the blood of its life.
For I will also demand an accounting for your lifeblood. I will demand it from every wild animal, and from humans: from each person I will demand an accounting for the life of his brother.”
“Whoever sheds human blood, his blood shall be shed in return for that blood, for I made humankind in the image of God.
“But you, be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and multiply upon it.
The Lord God spoke to Noah and to his sons who were with him and said:
“And behold, I establish my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,

“And with every living creature that is with you, among the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals of the earth that are with you, and among all that came out of the ark and all the animals of the earth.”
“I will establish my covenant with you. Never again shall all living creatures die from a flood, and never again shall there be a flood of water to destroy the whole earth.”
The Lord God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I will give between me and you and every living being that is with you, for everlasting generations.
I will set my rainbow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the everlasting covenant between me and the whole earth.
When I gather clouds over the earth, my rainbow shall appear in the clouds.
I will remember my covenant between me and you and every living being among all creatures. Never again shall there be a flood to destroy all living creatures.
My rainbow shall be in the clouds, and I will look at it to remember the everlasting covenant between me and every living being among all creatures that are on the earth.”
God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have made between me and you and every living creature that is on the earth.”
The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were Noah’s sons, and from them people spread throughout the whole earth.
And Noah, a farmer, began to cultivate the earth and planted a vineyard.
And he drank some of the wine, became drunk, and lay naked in his house.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and went out and told his two brothers outside.

And Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it across both their shoulders, and walked backward and covered their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father's nakedness.
And Noah sobered up from his wine and learned what his younger son had done to him, and he said:
“Cursed be Canaan, the child, and let him be a servant to his brothers.”
And he said, “Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant.
May God give Japheth room, and may he dwell in the house of Shem, and let Canaan be their servant.”
And Noah lived for three hundred and fifty years after the flood.
And all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
And these are the descendants of Noah's sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Elishah, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan were Elishah and Tarshish, the Kittites and the Rhodians.
And from these the islands of the nations were divided into their own lands, each according to its language, in their nations and their clans.
And the sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
And Cush fathered Nimrod. He began to be a giant on the earth.
And he was a giant hunter before the Lord God. Therefore they say, “Like Nimrod, a giant before the Lord God.”
And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land Asshur went out and built Nineveh, the city of Rehoboth, and Calah,
and Dasem, between Nineveh and Calah. This is the great city.
And Mizraim fathered the Ludim, the Seniim, the Salbiim, and the Naphtuhim,
and the Pathrusim and the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorim.
And Canaan fathered Sidon, his firstborn, and the Hittite,
and the Jebusite, the Amorite, and the Girgashite.
And the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites [?].
And the Arvadites [?], the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. After that, the families of the Canaanites spread out.
The territory of the Canaanites extended from Sidon toward Gerar and Gaza, and toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham, according to their families, their languages, their lands, and their nations.
Sons were also born to Shem, the father of all the descendants of Eber and the brother of Japheth the elder.
The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul [?], Gether, and Meshech.
Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber. The name of one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph [?], Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
And Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah.
And Obal, Abimael, and Sheba.
And Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
Their dwelling place extended from Mesha toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
These are the sons of Shem, according to their families, their languages, their lands, and their nations.
These are the families of Noah's sons, according to their generations and their nations. From these, the islands of the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.
And the whole earth had one language and one form of speech for everyone.
As they traveled from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
They said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and fire them.” They used brick instead of stone and bitumen instead of mortar.
They said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower whose top reaches heaven, and let us make a name for ourselves before we are scattered over the face of the whole earth.”
The Lord came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.
And the Lord said, “Look, they are one people, and they all have one language, and they have begun to do this. Now nothing they wish to do will be beyond their reach.”
“Come, let us go down and confuse their languages there, so that each one will not understand the speech of his neighbor.”
The Lord God scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city and the tower.
For this reason its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord God confused the languages of the whole earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
These are the generations of Shem. Shem was a hundred years old when he fathered Arpachshad, in the second year after the flood.
And after fathering Arphaxad, Shem lived five hundred years and had sons and daughters, and he died.
Arpachshad lived a hundred and thirty-five years and fathered Shelah.
After fathering Shelah, Arpachshad lived three hundred and thirty years and fathered sons and daughters, and he died.
And Shelah lived 130 years and fathered Eber.
And after fathering Eber, Shelah lived 330 years and fathered sons and daughters, and he died.
And Eber lived 134 years and fathered Peleg.
And after fathering Peleg, Eber lived 270 years and fathered sons and daughters, and he died.
And Peleg lived 134 years and fathered Reu.
And after fathering Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and fathered sons and daughters, and he died.
And Reu lived 132 years and fathered Serug.
And after fathering Serug, Reu lived 207 years and fathered sons and daughters, and he died.
And Serug lived 130 years and fathered Nahor.
And after fathering Nahor, Serug lived 200 years and fathered sons and daughters, and he died.
And Nahor lived 79 years and fathered Terah.
And after fathering Terah, Nahor lived 122 years and fathered sons and daughters, and he died.
And Terah lived 70 years and fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
These are the descendants of Terah: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.
And Haran died in the presence of his father Terah, in the land where he was born, in the land of the Chaldeans.
And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. The name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.
And Sarai was barren and bore no children.

And Terah took his son Abram, his son Nahor, Lot the son of his son Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of his son Abram, and brought them out of the land of the Chaldeans to go to the land of the Canaanites. And they came as far as Haran and settled there.
And all the days of Terah in Haran were 205 years, and Terah died in Haran.
And God said to Abram, “Leave your land, your kindred, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.
And I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed.
And I will bless those who bless you, and curse those who curse you, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed through you.”
And Abram went as God had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. And Abram was 75 years old when he left Haran.

And Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all their possessions that they had acquired, and all the people they had acquired in Haran. And they set out to go to the land of the Canaanites, and they came to the land of Canaan.
And Abram traveled through the length of the land as far as the place at Shechem, to the tall oak. But the Canaanites were living in the land at that time.
The Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “To your descendants I will give this land.” There Abram built an altar to the Lord, who had appeared to him.
He moved from there to the mountain east of Bethel and pitched his tent there, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the Lord and called on the name of the Lord.
Abram moved on, went away, and settled in the wilderness.
And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to live there as a foreigner, because the famine had become severe in the land.
When Abram was about to enter Egypt, he said to Sarah his wife, “I know that you are a beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife,’ and they will kill me but let you live.
Say, ‘I am his sister,’ so that things may go well for me because of you, and my life may be spared on your account.”
When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
Pharaoh’s officials also saw her and praised her before Pharaoh, and they took her into Pharaoh’s house.
They treated Abram well because of her, and he acquired sheep, cattle, donkeys, male and female servants, mules, and camels.
God punished Pharaoh and his household with great and terrible plagues because of Sarah, Abram’s wife.
Pharaoh called Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now, there is your wife before you. Take her and go away.”
He gave orders to men concerning Abram, to send him away with his wife and everything he had, and Lot with him.
Abram went up from Egypt into the wilderness, he and his wife and everything he had, and Lot with him.
Abram was very wealthy in livestock, silver, and gold.
He went back the way he had come, from the wilderness as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at first,
between Bethel and Ai, to the site of the altar he had made there at first. There Abram called on the name of the Lord God.
And Lot, who had gone with Abram, had cattle, sheep, and other livestock.
And the land was not sufficient for them to live together, because their possessions were great, and they could not live together.
There was a dispute between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. The Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land at that time.
Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no quarrel between me and you, or between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are brothers.
Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.”
Lot looked up and saw the whole region of the Jordan, which was entirely fertile. Before God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, it was like the garden of God and like the land of Egypt, as far as Zoar.
Lot chose for himself the whole region of the Jordan, and Lot moved away from the east. Each separated himself from his brother.
Abram lived as a foreigner in the land of the Canaanites, while Lot settled in one of the cities of the region and lived in Sodom.
The people of Sodom were very wicked and sinful before God.
After Lot had separated from him, God said to Abram, “Look up with your eyes, and from the place where you are, look north and south, east and west.
For I will give all the land that you see to you and to your descendants forever.
And I will make your descendants like the sand of the earth. If anyone can count the sand of the earth, then your descendants too can be counted.
Now rise and walk through the land, along its length and its breadth, for I will give it to you.
Abram moved on and came to live by the oak of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and there he built an altar to the Lord God.
And it happened during the reign of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of the nations:
They made war against Balak king of Sodom, Barsa king of Gomorrah, Sena king of Admah, Simobor king of Zeboiim, and the king of Balak, that is, Zoar.
All these gathered in the Valley of Salt, which is the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came and slaughtered the giants who were in Ashteroth-karnaim, the mighty nations who were with them, and the Sovmites in Shaveh, their city.
And they slaughtered the Horites who were in the mountains of Seir, as far as the terebinth of the valley, which is there in the wilderness.
Then they turned back and came to the Spring of Judgment, that is, Kadesh, and slaughtered all the rulers of Amalek and the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
The king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Balak, which is Zoar, went out and drew up their battle lines against them in the Valley of Salt:
Against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of the nations, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against five.
The Valley of Salt was full of pits of bitumen. The king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah fled and fell into them, while the rest fled to the mountainside.
They took all the plunder of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their provisions, and went away.
They also took Lot, Abram’s nephew, and his possessions, and went away, for he had been living in Sodom.
One of those who had escaped came and told Abram, who lived on the other side. He was living by the oak of Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and the brother of Aner, who were Abram’s allies.
When Abram heard that his nephew Lot had been taken captive, he counted those born in his household: three hundred and eighteen.
He pressed after them by night, he and his servants, and struck them as far as Hobah, which is to the left of Damascus.
He brought back all the plunder of Sodom, and he brought back his nephew Lot and all his possessions, as well as the women and the people.
The king of Sodom went out to meet him after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, in the Valley of Shaveh, that is, the Plain of the Kings.
Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine, for he was a priest of God Most High.
He blessed Abram and said, “Blessed is Abram by God Most High, who made heaven and earth.
Blessed is God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hands.” And he gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, and take the plunder for yourself.”
Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I raise my hand to God Most High, who made heaven and earth.
I will not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap from anything that is yours, so that you may not say, ‘I made Abram rich.’
Except for what the young men have eaten and the share of the men who came with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre—let them take their share.
After these things, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Abram. I will watch over you, and your reward will be very great.’
Abram said, ‘Lord, Lord, what will you give me? I am dying childless, and the son of Masek, my household-born servant, is Eliezer of Damascus.’
Abram said, ‘Since you have given me no offspring, my household-born servant will be my heir.’
And immediately the voice of God came to him and said, “This man will not be your heir, but the one who comes from you will be your heir.”
He brought him outside and said to him, ‘Look up at the heavens and count the stars, if you can count them.’ Then he said to him, ‘So shall your offspring be.’
Abram believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
He said to him, ‘I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Chaldeans to give you this land as an inheritance.’
Abram said, ‘Lord, Lord, how shall I know that I will inherit it?’
He said to him, ‘Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old male goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a pigeon.’
He took all these, cut them in half, and placed the halves opposite one another, but he did not cut the birds in half.
Birds came down upon their cut-up carcasses, and Abram sat beside them.
And near sunset a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and suddenly a terror of darkness came upon him.
It was said to Abram, ‘Know for certain that your offspring will be strangers in a land that is not theirs. They will be enslaved, mistreated, and oppressed for four hundred years.’
‘But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will come out here with many possessions.’
‘You will go to your fathers in peace, having reached a good old age.’
‘In the fourth generation they will return here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure.’
As the sun was setting, flames flashed, and behold, a smoking furnace and rays of fire passed between the cut-up pieces.
On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates,’
‘the Kenites, the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites,’
‘the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaim,’
‘the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.’
Sarai, Abram’s wife, bore him no children. She had an Egyptian servant girl whose name was Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram in the land of Canaan, ‘Since the Lord has prevented me from bearing children, go in to my servant girl, so that I may have a child through her.’ Abram listened to Sarai.
After Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years, Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant, and gave her to her husband Abram as a wife.
He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she was pregnant, her mistress became contemptible in her eyes.

And Sarai said to Abram, “The wrong done to me is your fault. I gave my maidservant into your arms, and now, when she saw that she had conceived, I became despised in her eyes. May God judge between me and you.”
And Abram said to Sarai, “Look, your maidservant is in your hands. Do to her whatever seems good to you.” And Sarai treated her harshly, and she fled from her.
The angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the road to Shur.
And the angel of the Lord said to her, “Hagar, Sarai’s maidservant, where have you come from, and where are you going?” And she said, “I have fled from Sarai, my mistress.”
The angel of the Lord said to her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.”
And the angel of the Lord said to her, “I will greatly multiply your descendants, and they will be too numerous to count.”
And the angel of the Lord said to her, “Look, you are pregnant, and you will bear a son and name him Ishmael, because the Lord has heard your distress.”
“And he will be a wild man; his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him, and he will live opposite all his brothers.”
And Hagar named the Lord who spoke to her, saying, “You are the God who looked upon me.” For she said, “I have indeed seen face to face the one who appeared to me.”
For this reason she called the well “The well of the one whom I saw face to face.” It is between Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar bore Abram a son, and he named his son, whom Hagar bore to him, Ishmael.
And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord God appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am your God. Be pleasing before me and be blameless.
And I will establish my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”
And Abram fell on his face, and God spoke with him, saying:
“As for me, here is my covenant with you: you will become the father of a multitude of nations.
Your name will no longer be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.
And I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings will come from you.
And I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your descendants after you.
And I will give to you and to your descendants this land in which you live as a foreigner, all the land of the Canaanites, as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God.
But you must keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you throughout their generations.
And this is my covenant, which you must keep, between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations:
Every male among you must be circumcised. You must circumcise the flesh of your foreskins, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and you.
Every male among you must be circumcised at eight days old, throughout your generations, whether born in the household or bought with silver from any foreigner who is not one of your descendants.
Those born in your house and those bought with your silver must certainly be circumcised. And my covenant will be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
The uncircumcised male who does not have the flesh of his foreskin circumcised on the eighth day—that person will be cut off from his people, because he has broken my covenant.”
And God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, her name will no longer be called Sarai, but her name will be Sarah.
And I will bless her and give you a son by her. And I will bless her, and she will become nations, and kings of nations will come from her.”
Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said in his heart, “Will a son be born to a hundred-year-old man? And will Sarah give birth at ninety?”
And Abraham said to God, “May this Ishmael live before you!”
And God said to Abraham, “Yes, Sarah your wife will bear you a son, and I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his descendants after him.”
“As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I will bless him and make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will father twelve nations, and I will make him a great nation.”
“But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”
And he finished speaking with him, and God went up from Abraham.

And Abraham took Ishmael his son, everyone born in his household, everyone he had bought with silver, and every male in Abraham’s household, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very day, as God had told him.
And Abraham was ninety and [?] years old when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.
And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.
On that very day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.
And he circumcised all the men of his household, those born in the household and those bought with silver from foreign nations.
And God appeared to him by the oak of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent at noon.
He lifted his eyes and looked, and there were three men standing above him. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed to the ground.
And he said, “Lord, if I have found favor before you, do not pass by your servant.”
“Let a little water be brought, and let them wash your feet, and refresh yourselves under this tree.”
“And I will bring bread, and you may eat, and afterward go on your way, since you have come to your servant.” And they said, “Do as you have said.”
And Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah and said to her, “Hurry, knead three measures of fine flour and make cakes.”
And Abraham ran to the herd and took a tender, good calf and gave it to the young man, urging him to prepare it quickly.
And he took butter and milk and the calf he had prepared and set them before them, and they ate. And he stood before them under the tree.
And they said to him, “Where is Sarah your wife?” He answered and said, “There she is, in the tent.”
And he said, “I will come back to you at this time, on these same days, and Sarah your wife will have a son.” And Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, for she was standing behind him.
And Abraham and Sarah were old and advanced in years, and Sarah had ceased to have the monthly periods of women.
Sarah laughed to herself and said, “Will what has not happened to me until now happen now? And my lord has grown old.”
And the Lord said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh to herself and say, ‘Will I really give birth, now that I am old?’”
“Can anything be impossible for God? At this time I will return to you, on these same days, and Sarah will have a son.”
Sarah denied it and said, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. And he said, “No, you did laugh.”
And the men rose from there and looked toward the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, and Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
And the Lord said, “Shall anything that I am going to do be hidden from Abraham my servant?”
“But Abraham will surely become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed through him.”

For I knew that he would command his sons and his household after him to keep the ways of the Lord and practice righteousness and justice, and that the Lord God would bring upon Abraham everything he had spoken to him.
And the Lord said, “The outcry of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah has increased, and their sins have become very great.
Now I will go down and see whether their actions match the outcry that reaches me, or not, so that I may know.”
The men turned from there and went to Sodom, while Abraham stood before the Lord.
Abraham approached and said, “Will you destroy the righteous along with the wicked? Will the righteous be treated like the wicked?
If there are fifty righteous people in the city, will you destroy them and not spare the whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous people who may be in it?

Far be it from you to do such a thing, to kill the righteous along with the wicked, so that the righteous are treated like the wicked! Far be it from you! You who judge the whole earth, do not pass such a judgment.”
And the Lord said, “If fifty righteous people are found in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
Abraham answered and said, “Now I have begun to speak to the Lord, though I am dust and ashes.”
“If the fifty righteous people fall short by five, will you destroy the whole city because of those five?” And he said, “I will not destroy it if forty-five are found there.”
He continued speaking to him and said, “What if forty are found there?” And he said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the forty.”
And he said, “Lord, would it offend you if I speak? What if thirty are found there?” And he said, “I will not destroy it if thirty are found there.”
And he said, “Since I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, what if twenty are found there?” And he said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the twenty.”
And he said, “Lord, would it offend you if I speak just once more? What if ten are found there?” And he said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten.”
The Lord departed when he had finished speaking with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his own place.
The two angels came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he rose to meet them and bowed with his face to the ground.

He said, “Here I am, my lords. Come into your servant’s house, rest, and let me wash your feet. Then you can rise early in the morning and go on your way.” And they said, “No, we will spend the night here in the city square.”
But he urged them strongly, and they turned aside to him and entered his house. He made them supper and baked unleavened bread for them, and they ate.
Before they had gone to sleep, the men of the city of Sodom surrounded the house, from the young to the old, all the people together.
They called Lot outside and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we may have sex with them.”
Lot went out to them outside the door and pulled the door shut behind him.
He said to them, “Far be it from you, brothers! Do not do this evil.

I have two daughters who have not had sex with a man. I will bring them out to you, and you may do with them whatever pleases you. Only do no harm to these men, because they have come under the shelter of my roof.”

And they said, “Stand aside! You came here to live as a foreigner, and now you would act as a judge? Now we will mistreat you even more than them.” They pressed hard against the man, Lot, and were close to breaking down the door.
But the men stretched out their hands, pulled Lot into the house with them, and shut the door of the house.
They struck the men who were outside the door of the house with blindness, from the least to the greatest, and they gave up searching for the door.
The men said to Lot, “Do you have anyone here—a son-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone else of yours in this city? Bring them out of this place.”
For we are going to destroy this city, because the outcry against its people has risen before the Lord, and the Lord has sent us to destroy it.

Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were going to marry his daughters, and said, “Get up and leave this place, for the Lord is destroying the city.” But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking.

When morning came, the angels urged Lot to hurry, saying, “Get up, take your wife and your two daughters who are with you, and leave here, so that you too do not perish because of the city’s wickedness.”

And they were distressed, and the angels took him by the hand, and his wife by the hand, and his two daughters by the hand, because the Lord had mercy on him. They brought him out and placed him outside the city.
When they had brought them outside, they said, “Save your life! Do not look back or stop anywhere in this region. Escape to the mountain, lest you be caught up with them.”
Lot said to them, “I beg you, Lord,
since your servant has found mercy in your sight, and you have shown great righteousness toward me by saving my life. But I cannot escape to the mountain, lest disaster overtake me and I die.
Look, this city is near enough to flee to, and it is small. Let me escape there—is it not small?—and my life will be preserved for your sake.”
He said to him, “Look, I have granted you this request as well: I will not destroy the city of which you have spoken.”
“And now hurry to escape there, because I cannot do anything until you arrive there.” For this reason he called the name of that city Zoar.
The sun rose over the earth, and Lot entered Zoar.
The Lord rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, from the Lord out of heaven,
and destroyed those cities, the entire surrounding region, all the inhabitants of the cities, and all the plants of the land.
Lot’s wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
Abraham went early in the morning to the place where he had stood before the Lord,
and looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and over the whole expanse of the surrounding land. He saw that flames were rising from the land like a whirlwind from a furnace.

When the Lord destroyed all the cities around the inhabited area, God remembered Abraham and brought Lot out, delivering him from the midst of the destruction, when the Lord destroyed the cities in which Lot had lived.
Lot went up from Zoar and lived in the mountain, with his two daughters, because he was afraid to live in Zoar. He lived there in a cave, with his two daughters.
And the older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no one on earth to come in to us as is the custom throughout the earth.”
“Come, let us give our father wine to drink and lie with him, and raise up offspring from our father.”
They gave their father wine to drink that night, and the older daughter went in and lay with her father that night. He did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day, the older daughter said to the younger, “Look, I lay with my father last night. Let us give him wine to drink tonight as well. Go in and lie with him, and let us raise up offspring from our father.”
And that night also they gave their father wine to drink, and the younger daughter went in and lay with her father. He did not know when she lay down or when she rose.
Both of Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab, saying, “From my father.” He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger daughter also gave birth to a son and named him Ammon, saying, “A son of my own kin.” He is the father of the Ammonites to this day.
Abraham moved from there to the southern land and settled between Kadesh and Shur, and stayed as a foreigner in Gerar.
Abraham said of Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” Abimelech, king of the people of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
God came to Abimelech in a vision at night and said, “You are about to die because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman.”
But Abimelech had not approached her, and he said, “Lord, will you destroy an innocent and righteous nation?”
“Did he not tell me, ‘She is my sister,’ and did she not tell me, ‘He is my brother’? I did this with a pure heart and innocent hands.”
And God said to him in the vision, “I knew that you did this with a pure heart, and I spared you from sinning against me. That is why I did not allow you to approach her.”
“But return the woman to her husband, for the man is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not return her, know that you will die, you and everyone who belongs to you.”
Abimelech rose early in the morning, called all his servants, and told them all these things. All the men were greatly frightened.

Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? Have we sinned against you in some way, that you have brought such great sins upon me and my kingdom? You have done to me something that no one should do.”
And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see that made you do this?”
Abraham said, “I thought, ‘Perhaps there is no reverence for God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’”
“But she really is my sister, the daughter of my father but not of my mother, and she became my wife.”
“When God brought me out of my father’s house, I said to her, ‘Do me this kindness: wherever we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
Abimelech took a thousand staters, cattle, sheep, male servants, and female servants, and gave them to Abraham. He also returned Sarah his wife to him.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “Look, my land is before you. Settle wherever you please.”
And he said to Sarah, “Look, I have given your brother a thousand staters. Let this be for the honor of your face and of all the women who are with you, and speak the truth in everything.”
Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, and they bore children.
For the Lord had firmly shut every womb in Abimelech’s household from the outside because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
The Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised.
Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the time God had told him.
Abraham named his son, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
Abraham circumcised his son Isaac on the eighth day, as the Lord God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears will rejoice with me.”
And she said, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse a child? For I have borne a son in my old age.”
And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day when his son Isaac was weaned.
Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, playing with her son Isaac.
She said to Abraham, “Drive out this slave woman and her son, for this slave woman’s son must not share the inheritance with my son Isaac.”
This matter greatly displeased Abraham because of his son.
And God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the child and the slave woman. Listen to Sarah in everything she tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be named.”
“But I will also make the slave woman’s son into a great nation, because he is your offspring.”

Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar. He placed the child on her shoulder and sent her away. She went and wandered in the wilderness near the Well of the Oath.
And the water in the skin ran out, and she cast the child under a fir tree.
She went and sat opposite him at a distance, about a bowshot away, for she said, “Let me not see the death of my son.” And she sat opposite him, and the child raised his voice and wept.

And God heard the child’s voice from the place where he was. God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, “What is the matter, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard your son’s voice from the place where he is.”
“Get up, take your child, and support him with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”
And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of fresh water. She went and filled the skin with water and gave the child a drink.
And God was with the child, and he grew and became an archer.
He lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech, Ochozath his palace overseer, and Phicol the commander of his army spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is with you in everything you do.”
“Now swear to me by God that you will not wrong me, my offspring, or my name, but that you will deal with me and with the land where you have been living according to the justice I have shown you.”
And Abraham said, “I swear.”
And Abraham reproached Abimelech about the well of water that Abimelech’s servants had taken away.
And Abimelech said to him, “I did not know who did this, and you did not tell me. I had not heard of it until today.”
Abraham took cattle and sheep and gave them to Abimelech, and the two made a covenant with each other.
And Abraham set seven ewe lambs apart.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What are these seven ewe lambs that you have set apart?”
And he said, “You shall take these seven ewe lambs from me, so that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well.”
For this reason he named that place the Well of the Oath, because there the two swore an oath to each other.
And there they made a covenant at the Well of the Oath. Abimelech, Ochozath his palace overseer, and Phicol the commander of his army rose and returned to the land of the Philistines.
And Abraham planted a tree by the Well of the Oath and there called on the name of the Lord, the everlasting God.
And Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for many days.
After these things, God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
And he said to him, “Take your beloved son, whom you love, Isaac, and go to the high land. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will tell you about.”
Abraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took with him two servants and his son Isaac. He split wood for the burnt offering, rose, and went to the place God had told him about.
On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey, while the boy and I go over there, worship, and return to you.”
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it on his son Isaac. He took the fire and the sword in his hand, and the two of them went on together.
Isaac said to Abraham his father, “Father!” And he said, “What is it, my son?” And he said, “Here is the fire, and here is the wood, but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”
He said, “God will provide himself a sheep for the burnt offering, my son.” The two of them went on together.
They came to the place God had told him about. Abraham built an altar there and laid the wood on it. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Abraham reached out his hand to take the sword and slaughter his son.
The angel of the Lord called to him from heaven and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He answered, “Here I am.”
He said, “Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God, since you have not spared your beloved son for my sake.”
Abraham looked up and saw a ram hanging by its horns from a Sabek tree. Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son Isaac.
Abraham named that place “The Lord Saw,” so that to this day people say, “On that mountain the Lord appeared.”
The angel of the Lord called to Abraham from heaven a second time and said:
“By myself I have sworn, says the Lord, because you have done this and have not spared your beloved son for my sake,
I will indeed bless you and multiply your descendants, making them as numerous as the stars of heaven and as the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the cities of their enemies.
All the nations of the earth will be blessed through your descendants, because you have obeyed my voice.”
Abraham returned to his young men, and they set out and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.
After these things, Abraham was told, “Milcah too has borne sons to your brother Nahor:
Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of the Syrians,
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These were the eight sons whom Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lived one hundred and twenty-seven years.
Sarah died in the city of Kiriath-arba, in the valley—that is, Hebron—in the land of the Canaanites. Abraham came to lament Sarah and mourn her.
Abraham rose from beside his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying:
“I am a stranger and a foreigner among you. Now give me a burial property among you, so that I may bury my dead.”
The sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying:
“Listen to us, my lord. You are a king from God among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs, for none of us will withhold the tombs from you.”
Abraham rose and bowed down to the people of the land, the sons of Heth.
Abraham spoke to them and said, “If you are willing for me to bury my dead out of my sight, listen to me and speak on my behalf to Ephron son of Zohar,
and let him give me the double cave that is at the edge of his field. Let him give it to me among you for its full worth in silver, as a possession for a resting place.”
Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth. Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth and everyone who entered the gate of his city,
and said, “Turn toward me, sir, and listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave in it. Before all my fellow citizens, I give it to you. Bury your dead.”
Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
He spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land and said, “Since you have heard me, listen to me. I will give you silver for the field. Take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.”
Ephron answered Abraham and said to him,
“No, my lord. I have heard that the land is worth four hundred silver staters. What is that between me and you? But you, bury your dead.”
When Abraham heard Ephron, he weighed out for Ephron the silver he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth: four hundred silver staters of a quality accepted by merchants.
So Ephron’s field beside the double cave, opposite Mamre—the field, the cave in it, and every tree in the field throughout all its boundaries—was confirmed
as Abraham’s possession before the sons of Heth who entered the gate of his city.
After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the double cave of the field opposite Mamre, that is, Hebron, in the land of the Canaanites.
The field and the cave in it were confirmed to Abraham by the sons of Heth as a burial property.
Abraham was old and advanced in years, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in everything.
Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his household, who was in charge of all his possessions, “Put your hand under my thigh,
and I will make you swear by the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I live.
Instead, you must go to my country, from which I came, and to my household, and take a wife from there for my son Isaac.”
The servant said to him, “Perhaps the woman will not be willing to come with me to this land. Should I then take your son back to the land from which you came?”
Abraham said, “Be careful not to take my son back there.

“The Lord, the God of heaven and the God of earth, who took me from my father’s house and from the land where I was born, who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to your descendants,’ will send his angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife from there for my son Isaac.”
If the woman is unwilling to come with you to this land, you will be released from this oath. Only do not take my son back there.”
Abraham’s servant put his hand under his master’s thigh and swore to him concerning this matter.
The servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed, taking with him some of all his master’s good things. He set out and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
He made the camels kneel outside the city beside the well of water, toward evening, when the water carrier came out.
He said, “Lord, God of my master Abraham, grant me success today, and show mercy to my master Abraham.
Here I stand beside this spring of water, and the daughters of the inhabitants of the city are coming out to draw water.

“Let the maiden to whom I say, ‘Lower your jar so that I may drink,’ and who says to me, ‘Drink, and I will also water your camels until they have finished drinking,’ be the one you have prepared for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown mercy to my master Abraham.”
Before he had finished speaking in his heart, Rebekah came out. She was born to Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor, and she had a jar on her shoulder.
The young woman was very beautiful, a virgin whom no man had known. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up.
The servant ran to meet her and said, “Give me a little water to drink from that jar.”
She said, “Drink, my lord.” She quickly lowered her jar onto her arms and gave him a drink.
When he had finished drinking, she said, “I will also draw water for your camels until they have all drunk.”
She quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw water. She drew water for all his camels.
The man watched her and remained silent, seeking to understand whether the Lord had made his journey successful or not.
When all the camels had finished drinking, the man took gold earrings, each weighing one daric, and two bracelets for her hands, weighing ten darics together.
He asked her, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me whether there is room in your house for us to stay.”
She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
She said to him, “We have plenty of straw and fodder, and room to stay.”
The man rejoiced and bowed down to God.

He said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld his righteousness and faithfulness from my master. The Lord has brought me successfully to the house of my master’s brother.”
The girl ran and told her mother’s household about these things.
Rebekah had a brother whose name was Laban, and Laban ran out to the man at the spring.

When he saw the earrings and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and heard the words of his sister Rebekah, who said, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man, who was standing beside his camels at the spring.
He said to him, “Come into the house, you who are blessed by the Lord. Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for your camels.”
The man went into the house and unloaded the camels. They gave straw and fodder to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of those who were with him.
They set food before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have said what I have to say.” They said, “Speak.”
He said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
“The Lord has greatly blessed my master, and he has become great. He has given him cattle and sheep, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
“Sarah, my master’s wife, bore my master a son after she had grown old, and he gave him everything he had.
“My master made me swear, saying, ‘You must not take a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites here, among whom I live as a foreigner in their land.’
“But you shall go to my father’s house and to my family, and take a wife from there for my son.”
“I said to my master, ‘Perhaps the woman will not come with me.’

He said to me, “The Lord my God, in whose presence I have been pleasing, will send his angel with you and make your journey successful. You will take a wife for my son from my family and from my father’s house.”
“‘Then you will be free from this curse of mine when you go to my family. If they will not give her to you, you will be free from this oath of mine.’
“When I came to the spring today, I said, ‘Lord, God of my master Abraham, if you have made this journey on which I have now come successful,

“‘Here I stand by this spring of water, and the daughters of the people of this city are coming out to draw water. Let it be the young woman to whom I say, “Give me a little water to drink from your jar.”’

And if she says to me, ‘Drink, and I will also draw water for your camels,’ she is the woman whom the Lord has appointed for his servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown mercy to my master Abraham.
And before I had finished speaking in my mind, Rebekah immediately came out, carrying a jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water, and I said to her, ‘Give me a drink.’
She quickly lowered her jar and said, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels water.’ So I drank, and she gave my camels water.
I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you? Tell me.’ She said, ‘I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son whom Milcah bore to Nahor.’ And I put earrings in her ears and bracelets on her hands.
I rejoiced and worshiped the Lord, and blessed the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who successfully guided me here on the path of truth to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
Now, if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me. But if not, let me know, so that I may turn to the right or to the left.
Laban and Bethuel answered, ‘This matter has come from the Lord, and we cannot say anything bad against what is good.’
Here is Rebekah before you. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, as the Lord has spoken.
When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the Lord.
The servant brought out gold objects, silver objects, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave gifts to her brothers and her mother.
He and the men who were with him ate and drank and slept. When they rose in the morning, he said, ‘Let me go, so that I may return to my master.’
Her brothers and her mother said, ‘Let the young woman stay with us for about ten days, and then she may go.’
He said to them, ‘Do not delay me, for the Lord has made my journey successful. Let me go, so that I may return to my master.’
Her brothers said, ‘Let us call the girl and ask her directly.’
They called Rebekah and said to her, ‘Will you go with this man?’ She said, ‘I will go.’
They sent away their sister Rebekah with her belongings, along with Abraham’s servant and those who were with him.
They blessed Rebekah and said to her, ‘You are our sister. May you become thousands and tens of thousands, and may your descendants possess the cities of your enemies.’
Rebekah and her maidservants rose, mounted the camels, and went with the man. The servant took Rebekah and departed.
Isaac was in the wilderness by the Well of the Vision, living in the land to the south.
Isaac went out to walk in the field toward evening. He looked up and saw ten camels coming.
Rebekah also looked up and saw Isaac, and she quickly got down from the camel.
