Their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, do this: take some of the produce of this land in your containers and bring the man gifts—resin, honey, incense, stacte, pistachios, and walnuts.
“Take twice as much money with you, and take back the money that was returned in your containers. Perhaps there was some mistake.
“Take your brother too, and get up and go down to the man.
“May my God grant you favor before the man, so that he sends your other brother and Benjamin back with you. But as for me, if I am deprived of my children, I am deprived of my children.”
The men took the gifts, twice as much money, and Benjamin. They got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
When Joseph saw them and his brother Benjamin, he said to the steward of his house, “Take these men into the house, slaughter animals, and make preparations, for these men will eat with me at noon.”
The man did as Joseph had said and brought the men into Joseph’s house.

When the men saw that they had been brought into Joseph's house, they said, “We are being brought in here because of the money that was returned in our containers the first time, so that they can search us, attack us, and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
They approached the man in charge of Joseph's house and spoke to him at the doorway.
They said, “Please, sir, we came down the first time to buy food.”
When we reached the lodging place and opened our sacks, each man's silver was in his own sack. We have now brought that silver back at its full weight, and here it is in our hands.
We have also brought other silver with us to buy food, and we do not know who put the silver in our sacks.

He said to them, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your fathers gave you treasure in your sacks. I have received your silver and am satisfied.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
The man brought the men into Joseph's house. Water was brought for them to wash their feet, and he gave their pack animals fodder.
They prepared their gifts before Joseph came at noon, because they had heard that he would dine there.
Joseph entered the house, and they presented him there with the gifts they had brought in their hands, and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.
He asked them, “How are you?” Then he said to them, “Is your elderly father well, the one you told me is still alive?”
They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” He said, “That man is blessed by God.” And they bowed down and paid him homage.
He looked up and saw Benjamin, his brother by the same mother, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, whom you said you would bring to me?” Then he said, “May God have mercy on you, my child.”
Joseph was deeply moved, and his heart ached for his brother. He sought a place to weep, went into his room, and wept there.
Then he washed his face and came out. He composed himself and said, “Serve the food.”
They served him by himself, the brothers separately, and the Egyptians who dined with him separately, because the Egyptians could not eat with Hebrews, for they were abhorrent to the Egyptians.
They sat before him, the firstborn according to his seniority and the youngest according to his youth, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.
They received their portions from him, and Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of theirs. They drank and became drunk with him.
Joseph gave orders to his steward, saying, “Fill the men's sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each man's silver at the mouth of his sack.”
“Put my silver cup in the youngest one’s sack, along with the money for his grain.” And it was done according to Joseph’s word, just as he had said.
When morning came, the men were sent away with their donkeys.
When they had left the city and had not gone far, Joseph said to his steward, “Get up and pursue the men. When you catch up with them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid good with evil?’”
“Why have you stolen the silver cup? Is this not the cup from which my master drinks and which he himself uses for divination? You have done an evil thing by doing this.”
When he found them, he spoke these words.
They said to him, “Why would our lord say such things? Far be it from your servants to do what you have said!
If we brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found in our sacks, how could we steal silver or gold from your master's house?
Now, whichever of your servants is found with the cup shall die, and we shall become our lord's slaves.”
He said, “Let it be as you have said: whoever is found with the cup shall be my slave, and you shall be innocent.”
They hurriedly lowered their loads to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
He searched, beginning with the eldest and finishing with the youngest, and found the cup in Benjamin's sack.
They tore their clothes, and each man put his load on his donkey, and they returned to the city.
Judah and his brothers came to Joseph while he was still there, and fell to the ground before him.
Joseph said to them, “What is this you have done? Do you not know that a man like me practices divination?”

Judah said, “What answer can we give our lord? What can we say, or how can we prove our innocence? God has discovered the wrongdoing of your servants. Now here we are, slaves of our lord, both we and the one with whom the cup was found.”
He said, “Far be it from me to do such a thing! The man with whom the cup was found shall be my slave, but you may go up in peace to your father.”
Judah approached him and said, “Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word before you. Do not be angry with your servant, for you are next to Pharaoh.”
“Lord, you asked your servants, saying, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
“We said to our lord, ‘We have an elderly father and a young boy, his youngest son, born in his old age. His brother died, and he alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’
“You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, and I will care for him.’
“We said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he leaves his father, he will die.’”
“You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you must not see my face again.’
“When we went up to your servant, our father, we told him the words of our lord.
“Our father said, ‘Go back and buy us a little food.’
“We said, ‘We cannot go down there unless our youngest brother goes down with us. Then we will go down, for we cannot see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
“Your servant, our father, said to us, ‘You yourselves know that my wife bore me two sons.’”
“‘One went away from me, and you said that he had been devoured by a wild beast. I have not seen him again to this day.’”
“‘Now if you take this one too away from me, and he falls ill on the journey, you will bring my old age down in sorrow to the realm of the dead.’
“Now if we go to your servant, our father, and the boy is not with us—his life is bound up with the boy’s life—
“when he does not see the boy with us, he will die, and your servants will bring the old age of your servant, our father, down in anguish to the realm of the dead.
“For your servant pledged himself as a guarantee for the boy to his father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, I will bear the blame before my father all my days.’
“Now let me, your servant, remain as my lord’s slave in place of the boy, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
“For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with us? Let me not see the calamity that will befall my father.”
Joseph could no longer restrain himself before all those standing around him. He said, “Send everyone away from me.” No one else was there with him when he made himself known to his brothers.
He wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard, and word reached Pharaoh’s household.
Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father really still alive?” His brothers could not answer him, because they were troubled in his presence.
Joseph said to his brothers, “Come close to me.” They came close, and he said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
“But do not grieve or be distressed because you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to save lives.
“For this is the second year of famine in the land, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
“God sent me ahead of you to leave you descendants on the earth and to sustain your many survivors.
“So it was not you who sent me here, but God. He made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his household, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.”
“Now hurry and go up to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt. Come down to me now, and do not delay.’”
“You shall live in the land of Goshen in Arabia and be near me—you, your sons, your sons’ sons, your sheep, your cattle, and everything you have.
“I will feed you there, for there are still five years of famine, so that you, your sons, and all your possessions may not perish.”
Look, your own eyes and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that it is my own mouth speaking to you.
Now tell my father about all my glory in Egypt and everything you have seen, and hurry to bring my father down here.
He fell on the neck of his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
He kissed all his brothers and wept over them. After that, his brothers spoke with him.
The news reached Pharaoh’s household, and they said, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: load up your baggage and go to the land of Canaan.
Take your father and your possessions and come to me. I will give you some of all the good things of Egypt, and you will eat the richest produce of this land.
You are to give this command: take wagons from the land of Egypt for your children and your wives, and take your father and bring him here.
Do not look longingly at your belongings, for the good things of the whole land of Egypt will be yours.’”
The sons of Israel did so, and Joseph gave them wagons according to the command of Pharaoh the king, and gave them provisions for the journey.
He gave each of them two robes, and to Benjamin he gave three hundred gold coins and five changes of robes.
Likewise, he sent his father ten donkey-loads of all the good things of Egypt, and ten mules loaded with provisions and food for his father on the journey.
He sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “Do not quarrel on the journey.”
They went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.
They told him, “Your son Joseph is alive, and he is ruler over the whole land of Egypt.” Jacob was astonished in his mind, for he did not believe them.
They told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to bring him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
Israel said, “It is a great thing for me if my son Joseph is indeed still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”
Israel set out with everything he had and came to Beersheba, where he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
God spoke to Israel in a vision at night and said, “Jacob, Jacob.” He said, “Who are you?”
He said, “I am the God of your fathers. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back up. Joseph will place his hands upon your eyes.”
Jacob rose and left Beersheba. The sons of Israel took Jacob their father, their belongings, and their wives in the wagons Joseph had sent to bring him.
They took their goods and all the possessions they had acquired in the land of Canaan and entered Egypt—Jacob and all his descendants with him.
His sons and his sons’ sons were with him, his daughters and his daughters’ daughters; he brought all his descendants into Egypt.
These are the names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Jacob’s firstborn was Reuben.
The sons of Reuben were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
And the sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
And the sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And the sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan, and the sons of Perez were Hezron and Jemuel.
The sons of Issachar were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
And the sons of Zebulun were Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, along with his daughter Dinah. His sons and daughters numbered thirty-three people in all.
The sons of Gad were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
These were the children of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah. The sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah. She bore these to Jacob: sixteen sons.
And the sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife, were Joseph and Benjamin.

And Joseph’s sons born in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore him, were Manasseh and Ephraim. And Manasseh’s son, whom the Syrian concubine bore him, was Machir, and Machir fathered Gilead. And the sons of Ephraim, Manasseh’s brother, were Shuthelah and Tahan, and Shuthelah’s son was Edem.
And Benjamin’s sons were Bela, Becher, and Ashbel. And Bela’s sons were Gera, Naaman, Anachis, Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Gera fathered Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel, whom she bore to Jacob: eighteen people in all.
And the sons of Dan were Hushim.
And the sons of Naphtali were Asiel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel. She bore these to Jacob: seven people in all.
And all the people who entered Egypt with Jacob, who were descended from him, excluding the wives of Jacob’s sons, numbered sixty-six people in all.
And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt numbered two people. All the people of Jacob’s household who entered Egypt numbered seventy-five.
And he sent Judah ahead to Joseph, so that Joseph would meet him at Heroonpolis in the land of Rameses. He himself came to the land of Goshen.
Joseph prepared his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father at Heroonpolis. When he appeared before him, he fell on his neck and wept bitterly.
And Israel said to Joseph, “Now I can die, since I have seen your face and you are still alive.”
And Joseph said to his brothers and his father’s household, “I will go and tell Pharaoh, ‘My brothers and my father’s household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
The men are shepherds and keepers of livestock, and they have brought their livestock, their cattle, and everything they own here.’
Now, if Pharaoh calls you and says, ‘What is your occupation?’

you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers,’ so that you may live in the land of Goshen, because every shepherd is detestable to the Egyptians.”
And Joseph came and told Pharaoh, saying, “My father and my brothers, their flocks and cattle, and everything they own have come from the land of Canaan, and they are now in Goshen.”
And he took five men from among his brothers with him and presented them before Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph’s brothers, “What is your occupation?” They said to Pharaoh, “Your servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers.”

And they said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as foreigners in this land, because there was no pasture for your servants’ flocks, for the famine grew severe in the land of Canaan. So now let your servants settle in the land of Goshen.”
And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph and said, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.

Look, the land of Egypt is before you. Settle your father and your brothers in good land, and let them live in the land of Goshen. If you know that there are capable men among them, put them in charge of my livestock.”
And Joseph brought in Jacob his father and presented him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many years have you lived?”

Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The years of my life spent as a stranger are one hundred and thirty. The years of my life have been few and difficult, and they have not reached the years my fathers lived as strangers.”
Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from his presence.
Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a place to live in the land of Egypt, in good land in the region of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
And Joseph supplied his father, his brothers, and his father’s entire household with grain, according to the number of mouths.
There was no food anywhere in the land, because the famine had become very severe. The land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.
Joseph collected all the money found in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan in exchange for the grain he sold, providing them with food. Joseph brought all the money into Pharaoh’s house.
When the money ran out in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, “Give us bread. Why should we die before you? Our money has run out.”
Joseph said to them, “Bring your livestock, and I will give you bread in exchange for your livestock, if your silver has run out.”

And they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for horses, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. And he fed them with bread in exchange for all their livestock during that year.

That year ended, and they came to Joseph in the second year and said to him, “May we not be destroyed by our lord! If there was money, it has run out, and our livestock and possessions are with you, my lord. Nothing remains to us before our lord except our bodies and our land.”

“Now, so that we do not die before you and our land is not ruined, buy us and our land in exchange for bread. We and our land will belong to Pharaoh as slaves. Give us seed so that we may sow and live, and not die, and so that our land may not be ruined.”
Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, because the Egyptians sold their land to Pharaoh, for the famine had become severe upon them. So the land became Pharaoh’s.
He made the people his slaves, from one end of Egypt’s borders to the other.

The priests’ land was an exception, for Joseph did not buy it. Pharaoh regularly gave provisions to the priests, and they ate the provisions Pharaoh gave them. For that reason they did not sell their land.
Joseph said to all the Egyptians, “Look, today I have bought you and your land for Pharaoh. Take seed for yourselves and sow the land.”
“When it yields a harvest, you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh. The other four parts shall be yours, for seed for the land and for food for yourselves, all your households, and your children.”
They said, “You have kept us alive. We have found favor before our lord, and we will be Pharaoh’s slaves.”
Joseph established a law for them in the land of Egypt, lasting to this day, that a fifth should be given to Pharaoh. The priests’ land alone was excepted, because it did not belong to Pharaoh.
Israel settled in the land of Egypt, in the region of Goshen. They acquired property there, grew, and became very numerous.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years. The years of Jacob’s life were one hundred and forty-seven.

When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called his son Joseph and said to him, “If I have found favor before you, put your hand under my thighs and show me kindness and faithfulness: do not bury me in Egypt.”
“But I will lie down with my fathers, and let them carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their tomb.” And he said, “I will do as you say.”
He said, “Swear to me.” And he swore to him. Then Israel bowed in worship over the top of his staff.
After these things, Joseph was told, “Your father Jacob is ill.” Joseph took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, with him and came to Jacob.
Jacob was informed, and they said, “Look, your son Joseph is coming to you.” And Israel gathered his strength and sat up in bed.
Jacob said to Joseph, “My God appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me.”
And he said to me, “Look, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make you into an assembly of nations, and I will give you this land as an everlasting inheritance.”
“Now your two sons who were born in Egypt before I came to Egypt are mine. Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are.
Any other children you father after these shall be yours. They shall be called by their brothers’ names in their inheritances.

When I was coming from Mesopotamia in Syria, your mother Rachel died in the land of Canaan, as I approached the stretch of land of Chabratha on the way to Ephrath. I buried her on that stretch of land—that is Bethlehem.”
When Israel saw Joseph’s sons, he said, “Who are these to you?”
Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God gave me here.” And Jacob said, “Bring them to me so that I may bless them.”
Israel’s eyes had grown dim from old age, and he could not see. Joseph brought them to him, and he kissed them and took them in his arms.
Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I have not been deprived of seeing your face, and God has also shown me your offspring.”
Joseph took them away from his knees, and they bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.
Joseph took his two sons, Ephraim on his right, at Israel’s left, and Manasseh on his left, at Israel’s right, and brought them to him.
Israel stretched out his right hand and placed it on Ephraim’s head, though he was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh’s head. He crossed his hands, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
He blessed them and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac were pleasing, the God who has fed me from my childhood until this day,

the angel who rescued me from every evil, may he bless these children. May my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac be called upon them, and may they be blessed to become a very great multitude upon the earth.”
When Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head, he was displeased. Joseph took hold of his father’s hand to move it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
Joseph said to his father, “Not that way, father, for this one is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.”

But his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know. He too shall become a people, and he too shall be exalted. But his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations.”
He blessed them that day and said, “Through you Israel shall pronounce blessings, saying, ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’” And he placed Ephraim before Manasseh.
Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I am dying, but God shall be with you and shall bring you back to the land of your fathers.
I have given you Shechem as your own possession, beyond what your brothers receive, which I took from the hands of the Amorites with my sword and bow.”
Jacob called his sons and said, “Gather together so that I may tell you what will happen to you in the last days.
Gather together and listen, sons of Jacob; listen to Israel, your father.
Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the first of my sons. You walked in harshness, and with harsh arrogance you brought dishonor.
Do not boil over like water, for you went up to your father’s bed. Then you defiled the bed you went up to.
Simeon and Levi are brothers; they carried out injustice of their own will.
May my soul not enter their council, and may my mind take no pleasure in their assembly, for in their anger they killed men, and in their own desire they hamstrung bulls.
Cursed be their anger, for it was brazen, and their wrath, for it was fierce. I will divide them among Jacob and scatter them among Israel.
Judah, your brothers will praise you. Your hands will be on the backs of your enemies; your father's sons will bow down to you.
Judah is a lion's cub. From a shoot you came up, my son. You came up, reclined, and slept like a lion and like a lion's cub. Who will rouse him?
A ruler shall not be lacking from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things appointed for him come; and he is the expectation of the nations.
He will tie his foal to a vine and his donkey's foal to a vine tendril. He will wash his robe in wine and his clothes in the blood of grapes.
His eyes are bright with wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
Zebulun shall dwell by the seashore, and he shall be a harbor for ships, and shall extend as far as Sidon.
Issachar desired what was good, resting between the allotted lands.
He saw that rest was pleasant and that the land was fertile. He put his shoulder to work and became a productive man.
Dan will judge his people like one man among Israel.
And Dan will be a snake lying in wait on the road, striking the horse's heel and throwing its rider backward.
And to await the salvation of the Lord.
Gad will go out against a band, and he himself will go out with a band in pursuit of them.
Asher's bread will be rich, and he himself will provide food for rulers.
Naphtali is a tall tree, making produce grow, clothing beauty with produce.
Joseph is a flourishing son, a flourishing, envied son. My young son, turn to me.
Slanderers spoke ill of him and denounced him, and bowmen bore a grudge against him.
And their bows were shattered by force, and the sinews of their arms were loosened by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob, from him who strengthened Israel.
From the God of your father; and my God helped you and blessed you with the blessing of heaven above and the blessing of the earth, full of everything, because of the blessings of breasts and womb.

The blessings of your father and your mother, which surpassed the blessings of the everlasting mountains and the blessings of the eternal hills, shall be upon Joseph’s head and upon the head of the brothers whom he led.
Benjamin is a ravenous wolf. In the morning he will still be eating, and toward evening he will distribute food.
All these are the sons of Jacob, twelve tribes. And this is what their father said to them, and he blessed them; he blessed each of them according to his own blessing.
And he instructed them and said to them, “I am being gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
in the cave in the field there at Machpelah, opposite Mamre, in the land of the Canaanites, the cave that Abraham acquired from Ephron the Hittite as a burial property.

There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; there they buried Leah, in the property consisting of the field and the cave in it, acquired from the sons of Heth.”
And Jacob finished instructing his sons, drew his feet up into the bed, died, and was gathered to his people.
And Joseph fell upon his father's face, wept over him, and kissed him.
And Joseph ordered his servants, the embalmers, to wrap his father, and the embalmers wrapped Israel.
Forty days were completed for him, for that was how the days for burial were counted, and Egypt mourned for him for seventy days.
When the days of mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s officials and said, “If I have found favor with you, speak to Pharaoh and say:
‘My father made me swear an oath, saying, “Look, I am dying. Bury me there in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now let me go up and bury my father, and I will return.’”
Pharaoh said, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear.”
Joseph went up to bury his father. All Pharaoh’s servants, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of Egypt went up with him.
Also accompanying him were Joseph’s entire household, his brothers, and his father’s entire household. They left their relatives, sheep, and cattle in the land of Goshen.
Chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and they formed a very large company.
They reached the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented him with very great and intense lamentation. He mourned his father for seven days.

The inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad and said, “This is a great mourning for the Egyptians.” Therefore it was named “Mourning of Egypt.” It is beyond the Jordan.
The sons of Israel did for him as he had commanded them.

They lifted him up and buried him there, and his sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the double cave that Abraham had acquired as a burial property from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.
Joseph returned to Egypt, together with his brothers and everyone who had gone up with him to bury his father.
When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father had died, they said, “Perhaps Joseph will bear a grudge against us and repay us for all the evil we inflicted on him.”
They came to Joseph and said, “Your father made us swear before he died, saying:

‘Say this to Joseph: “Forgive them their offenses and their sins, for they inflicted evil on you.”’ Now forgive the offenses of the servants of your father’s God.” Joseph wept because of the words they spoke to him.
His brothers came to him, fell down before him, and said, “Look, we are your servants.”
And Joseph said to them, “Do not be afraid, for I too belong to God.”
“You intended evil against me, but God intended good for me, as has indeed happened this very day, so that I might feed many people.” And he said to them:
“Do not be afraid. I will feed you and your households.” He comforted them and reassured their hearts.
Joseph lived in Egypt, together with his brothers and his father’s entire household. Joseph lived for one hundred and ten years.
Joseph saw Ephraim’s children down to the third generation, and the children of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s lap.
Joseph spoke to his brothers and said, “Look, I am dying. God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land that God swore to give to our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying, “When God visits you, bring my bones up from here with you as well.”
Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They buried him and placed him in a coffin in Egypt.
